fields.narrative: Fired four torpedoes, 80 starboard track, 1100 yards, GA 15 L. At time of firing had TBT bearings, periscope bearings, SJ bearings and ranges, all checking. Two hits seen from the bridge, both duds. Nothing heard below decks. No doubt about the hits the first was aft of the midship superstructure, and the second was on the bow. Immediately afterward, flashlights were seen on deck and over the side at the points where the torpedoes hit. The target swung towards to ram and we went to full speed and swung away. Lights all over his decks by this time.

fields.narrative: fired 4 torpedoes, 130 port track, 1000 yards, GA 0. 45 seconds later saw and heard one hit on stern. Eight seconds later sound reported another hit, but not seen through periscope (maybe another dud). However, the effect of the single hit was remarkable. Target sank in two minutes, by the stern. All hands in conning tower got a look.

fields.event: [SUMMARY] Sighted convoy of 3 tankers and 3 freighters with air escort, zigzagging 030°T to 130°T, speed 8. Unable to close.
[SUMMARY] Identified convoy: NIPPON MARU type tanker, SYOYO MARU and SAN PEDRO MARU types; freighters LIMA MARU, ARGUN MARU, KOHUKU MARU.
Lost sight contact.
Surfaced. Full speed on all engines.
Radar contact. Commenced working around on starboard side of convoy. It is still fairly light, and lookouts picked up the convoy at about 8000 yards range.
[SUMMARY] On starboard beam, range 8000, convoy course 080 T, speed 8. Two columns of 3 ships on PPI. Tankers on near side.
Commenced surface approach, planning to fire three torpedoes at the first ship, three at the second, then swing and fire four at the third ship.
Nearest column of ships in plain sight - THREE TANKERS, with the big one leading. It is still fairly light. They should see us but they don't.

fields.narrative: During this time we were swinging hard left. Bridge saw FREIGHTER #3 turn away. FREIGHTER #1 was holding on her original course. Both remaining freighters and tankers opened fire. Range was about 1000 yards to the tanker column, 2000 yards to the freighter column. It was so bright they had no difficulty seeing us. Splashes were seen on both sides of us, but not too close. TANKER #3 presented a 50 starboard angle on the bow, and was closing rapidly, firing his bow gun. We seemed to take a year to pick up speed. Finally steadied with our stern toward him, and at fired three torpedoes aft at this tanker, 50 S track, GA 0, 1000 yards. All missed, probably because we had not steadied enough, and he was swinging toward us, as we realized in a moment.

We were making full speed by this time, and pulling away. However, he continued firing, and was getting a little better, as was evidenced by shells whistling overhead.

fields.event: [SUMMARY] Dived. CO fell into periscope well as quartermaster lowered periscope; CO supported on elbows and halted descent.
One violent explosion.
Another violent explosion. Both sounded like ships sinking. No depth charges were dropped at any time during these attacks.
[SUMMARY] Periscope depth; took periscope pictures of burning tanker. Reloaded, two torpedoes left forward, four aft.
Reload completed.

[SUMMARY] Surfaced. Five radar/PPI contacts. TANKER #1 stopped burning, TANKER #2 burning, TANKER #3 down by bow, FREIGHTER #1 undamaged stopped, FREIGHTER #2 sunk, FREIGHTER #3 undamaged heading north.
[SUMMARY] Pursued FREIGHTER #3; observed vertical stern of sinking ship (believed TANKER #3) silhouetted against burning NIPPON MARU.
The stern went under. At this time the whole hull of TANKER #1 could be seen, red hot.
Attained surface firing position on FREIGHTER # 3. So bright we nearly dived, but decided to ride our luck.

fields.narrative: Fired last two bow torpedoes, 90 S track, GA 0, 1400 yards. Two hits in the bow, target immediately went down by the bow, and we left him in an apparently sinking condition. As we swung left he opened fire. A light came on on his bridge and he commenced signalling. With this, FREIGHTER # 1 opened fire also. While we circled, it seemed there were flashes of gunfire all around us. Shooting still pretty wild.

Although no definite proof, from firing data feel sure we must have hit, and hence at least one dud. Pulled out again and thought it over. We have only two torpedoes left, both aft, and he is getting pretty handy with his gun.

fields.narrative: Fired last two torpedoes, 90 port track, GA 0, 1000 yards. One hit, one missed, according to sound. No detonation, but target evidently felt the hit, for he opened fire immediately. The feelings of the Commanding Officer and the control party by this time can be imagined. Held huddle over a battle surface, decided against it, because our three inch deck gun has never in its history fired five consecutive shots without jamming. We felt, under the circumstances, that our chances in a gun fight against a fully aroused enemy were not of the best, and that the probability of the target's sinking eventually was still good.

[SUMMARY] TANKER #2 blew up in brilliant flame; two huge fires visible. Crew permitted on bridge to view fires.
